$comment: V-80 and A15. Transferred kilobytes for a cold load at 390x844, per route, and the landing's height. BUDGETS WERE RECORDED ON 6 OCTOBER 2026 FOR THE EIGHT PUBLIC ROUTES. Until then every budget was null, and a null budget is reported and never fails, so this check printed 'weight: within budget' against fifteen nulls and could not fail at all. It can fail now: dropping a budget under a route's weight was tried and the script exited 1. HOW THESE NUMBERS WERE ARRIVED AT, because the obvious way is wrong. A single measurement is not a budget: the same production build, measured five times against the same server, moved by 6 KB on /guides/avoiding-rental-scams and by 77 KB on /welcome (660, 660, 664, 734, 737). A budget set near one reading would have gone red on the next run and taught everyone to raise it. Each budget is therefore the HIGHEST weight seen for that route across five local passes and CI's own run (37398903073, front-door job 112061355933), plus the larger of 20 KB and that route's observed spread, rounded up to 5 KB. Observed max and spread per route: / 525 and 28; /welcome 737 and 77; /sign-in 668 and 17; /sign-up/email 677 and 21; /check 610 and 18; /move-in-cost 475 and 13; /for-agents 552 and 14; /guides/avoiding-rental-scams 458 and 6. A regression worth catching is a webfont, an image or a library and costs 40 KB and up, so these still catch one. THE VARIANCE ITSELF IS A DEFECT AND THESE BUDGETS ARE LOOSER THAN THEY SHOULD HAVE TO BE. The likeliest cause is `waitUntil: 'networkidle'` in check-weight.mjs settling at different points while lazy assets are still arriving, which would make the spread an artefact of the measurement rather than the page. Worth fixing in the script, after which every budget here can come down. /for-agents HAD looked like a CI-versus-local difference and is not one: CI read 552 once (run 37398903073) and 482 the next time (run 37408766620) on the same code, against 483 to 497 in a container. So that 55 KB was variance inside CI, not an environment gap, and nobody should go looking for a build difference that is not there. Its budget stays 575 because 552 remains the highest reading ever seen for it, which is what the rule above asks for. Deliberately NOT the 'measured minus 20 percent' that `check-weight.mjs --record` writes: that would have put all eight routes over budget on the first run, turning CI red with no fix attached, and reducing page weight is not the release session's work to do unasked. The 20 percent diet remains the right target for whoever owns page weight. Ratchet down, never up without a reason in the commit. THE SEVEN SIGNED-IN ROUTES ARE STILL NULL, AND THAT IS HONEST RATHER THAN UNFINISHED: CI skips them for want of a WEIGHT_COOKIE, and the only cookie obtainable without credentials comes from `tests/gate-stub-session.mjs`, whose stub serves nothing, so the pages render empty and not-found states and their weight is not the weight of the page. They can be budgeted the first time CI mints a WEIGHT_COOKIE from real QA credentials, and not before. /wallet was retired on 25 September and is gone from the list. Heights are a ratchet too: the UIUX item 9 targets are under 8,000px at 390 and under 6,500px at 1440, and the landing is above both. The front-door re-audit of 30 September measured 9,728 and 8,658; this check now reads 9,455 and 8,627, so the ceiling holds that height and must only come down.
